info.description:
civex is a local-first research data management system: schemas, records, files, and workflow automation in one place, running on your own machine against your own database.

Every endpoint below is served under the `/api` prefix (e.g. `GET /api/schemas`); paths in this reference omit that prefix for brevity.

## Errors

Errors share one envelope shape across the API. Domain errors (not found, already exists, validation, misconfiguration) return a 4xx/5xx status with a JSON body of `{"detail": "<message>"}`. Request body/query validation failures return 422 with `{"detail": "Request validation failed", "errors": [...]}`, one entry per invalid field. Anything unexpected returns a generic 500 with `{"detail": "Internal server error", "request_id": "<id>"}` — the same id echoed on the `x-request-id` response header, for correlating with server logs.

See the [getting started guide](https://civexdata.github.io/civex-docs/getting-started/install.html) for installing the CLI and standing up your first project.

Download the picked files that are only on the server to this computer
(onto their collection's drive). Answers when they have arrived: how many
came and which the server hasn't got yet.

Build the selection as a folder tree on the server's machine.

`link` makes a folder on the drive holding most of the files: read-only
hard links to the files there, and copies of any it can't link (on another
drive, or a drive without links); `copy` makes copies on the drive named by
`volume`. Answers 409, building nothing, when files are out of reach
(`files_unavailable`, unless `allow_partial`) or the drive can't be written
to (`links_not_possible`). Building again into the same folder updates
it.

post.description:
Delete export folders: the links or copies the export made, then the
folder. A link is removed without touching the stored file it points at.
Files in the folder that the export didn't make are left, with the folder.
A path that isn't an export folder is refused (listed under `errors`).

A page of a selection's files, one row per file as stored (a file
several records use is one row: `uses` lists those records, each with the
names of the records above it, `trail`; `others` counts the records
outside the selection that use it too), each with where it is (`place`: a
drive's name, `server` or `missing`; `place_kind`: drive, unreachable,
server or missing), narrowed by place, name (the name a file was added
under, or its record or one above it, found as a search of records finds
them) and the selection's own filter; and `summary`, where all of the
selection's files are, by place. The counts and the order come from the
database alone, so a page costs the same whatever it is a page of; only
its rows are named. While this project follows a
server, each file says whether the server has it (`sent`), `server`
counts them (`sent`, and `unsent`: on a drive here, not sent yet), and
`server` in the request narrows to either. Counts are of files.

Remove this computer's copies of the picked files to free space; each
comes back when opened or exported. Only files the server confirms it
holds, and never one a collection kept on this computer uses (switch that
collection to fetch when opened first). Counts unless `dry_run=false`.

Move the picked files onto one drive: a selection's files, narrowed by
place, name or ticked files (`shas`). Only those move; the rest of their
collections stay where they are. Files only on the server are downloaded
first; files on a drive that can't be reached, or missing, are left out. It
runs like any other move (one at a time, safe to pause, cancel or lose
power; see /store/transfers). Files downloaded straight onto the drive need
no move: when nothing else has to move, `transfer_id` is null and
`downloaded` says how many came. Every file picked goes, whoever else uses
it: one on a drive that is the home of a collection using it is copied,
so the home keeps it (`plan.copied`). With `dry_run`, only `plan` is
answered and nothing is done. 422 when they are all already there.

post.description:
Try a workflow (saved or not: the YAML is sent) on one record without
keeping anything: it runs as a real run would, inside a transaction that is
always rolled back, and the answer says what it would have done (each
record created, changed or deleted, with the values before and after, and
the runs its saves would start). JSON `{content, record_id}`, or a form
with those plus the files for each `files` input. Works whether the
workflow is on or off, and while automation is paused. 422 when the YAML
doesn't pass its checks or the record isn't the kind it runs on; a step
that fails is not an error but `ok: false` with `error`.

Try a workflow on several records at once, keeping nothing: each is
tried as `POST /workflows/try` would, one after the other, and all of it is
rolled back. Names no records and it takes the most recently changed
records of the kind the workflow runs on (`sample`, 5 by default), so an
editor can show what a change would do without anyone choosing. JSON
`{content, record_ids, sample}`, or a form with those (`record_ids`
repeated) plus the files for each `files` input, given to every trial. A
record it can't run on is answered with `problem`, not an error.

Run one workflow on several records: one queued run per record, in one
request, one commit and one pass of the worker. A record that is missing, or
is not the schema the workflow is for, is listed under `skipped` with the
reason and the rest are still queued. A workflow that asks for files cannot
be run this way (422): the files differ per run. Refused (422) while
automation is paused.

patch.description:
Switch a workflow on (its triggers start runs) or off (it runs only when
someone starts or tries it). Only the file's `enabled:` line changes. 422
when the workflow no longer passes its checks.
